_README: Verified plausible price bands per ticker, read off accredited external
sources. These exist because local continuity alone cannot decide which of
two conflicting price levels is real when corruption alternates: SMER spends
355 days at ~3.00 and 200 days at ~0.30 across 2019-2021, switching 48 times,
so flank-relative logic yields contradictory corrections for adjacent runs.
A band is the range the stock genuinely traded in during that window. A run
whose median falls OUTSIDE the band, and which a single power of ten brings
INSIDE it, is a decimal-shift correction. Everything else is left alone.
CRITICAL: low price does NOT imply corruption. HAFR and NBV genuinely traded
below 1.00 KES for years - their bands say so explicitly, which is what stops
a fixer from multiplying real prices tenfold.
Add a ticker here only after checking a real source. Unanchored tickers are
reported for review and never auto-corrected.
SUPERSEDED WHERE THE ARCHIVE COVERS. The NSE all-stocks archive
(~/Documents/archive, 2007-01-02 to 2025-10-31) gives the exchange's own
printed close per ticker per date. Where it covers a date, prefer it and
prefer apply_archive_corrections.py, which copies exact figures instead of
inferring from a band.
These bands were read off chart axes by eye and one of them was WRONG: the
original EQTY entry said 4.0-30.0 for 2007 when the exchange printed a
median of 130.00. MarketScreener back-adjusts for share splits, so reading
it to band a RAW series understates pre-split years by the split factor.
Treat every band here as approximate, and as a fallback for dates the
archive does not reach.

SMER.name: Sameer Africa Plc
SMER.note: Chart axis floor is 1.5; never traded near 0.30. The ~0.30 series is corruption, the ~3.00 series is real.

TOTL.name: TotalEnergies Marketing Kenya Plc
TOTL.note: Trades 20-45 KES. Never near 1.28 or 3.50 - those runs are corruption. MA(200)=23.66, current 43.40.

HAFR.name: Home Afrika Limited
HAFR.note: GENUINELY SUB-1 for years. Chart tooltip Oct-2021 reads O 0.40 H 0.40 L 0.36 C 0.40. The ~10-12 runs in 2017-2018 are the corruption (real level ~1.0-1.2), NOT the low prices.

NBV.name: Nairobi Business Ventures Plc
NBV.note: GENUINELY SUB-1 in 2018-2020 (~0.3-0.6), then a real spike to ~10 in 2021 and a long decline to 1.38. The sub-1 prices are REAL and must not be multiplied.

EQTY.name: Equity Group Holdings Plc
note: CORRECTED. The earlier band here was read off a MarketScreener chart and
was wrong: it said 4.0-30.0 for 2006-2007. The archive shows EQTY
actually traded 74.50-276.00 that year, median 130.00, then fell to a
median of 14.60 in 2009 at its 1:10 share split.
The chart misled because MarketScreener back-adjusts for splits, so it
renders pre-2009 prices at a tenth of what the exchange printed. Reading
an adjusted chart to band a raw series is not sound, and this entry is
the proof.
Bands below come from the archive's own yearly medians. Where the archive
covers a date it supersedes any chart-derived band.

KPLC.name: Kenya Power and Lighting Company Plc
note: SPLIT-AWARE BANDS. KPLC executed a 1:7 share split on 2010-01-07:
the raw NSE series steps 140.00 -> 19.90 that day, which is a REAL
corporate action and must never be 'corrected'. The band boundary is
placed exactly on that date so pre-split prices in the hundreds are
recognised as genuine.
MarketScreener back-adjusts for the split, so its chart shows ~15-25
for 2007-2009 while raw NSE printed 200+. Bands below follow the RAW
series, not the adjusted chart. From 2011 onward the two agree - the
chart's Sep-2013 close of 14.35 matches the raw 2013 median of 14.95.
The 2020-2023 trough near 1.2-2.0 is REAL and is banded as such, so it
cannot be multiplied up. Verified on the chart, which bottoms near 1.2.
Two genuine corruptions sit inside 2010 and are caught by these bands:

CARB.name: Carbacid Investments plc
reason: DO NOT auto-correct. CARB's anomalies are NOT decimal shifts.
Through 2014-2015 the raw series alternates between ~20-27 and ~75-89
dozens of times, at a consistent ratio of roughly 3.3-4.0 - never a
power of ten. The 2018 episodes behave the same way (10.90 -> 2.70 ->
11.55 -> 2.80, ratio ~4.0). No power-of-ten correction can express that,
so the band mechanism would either do nothing or do something wrong.
The raw and adjusted series also fail to reconcile: MarketScreener's
Feb-2010 close is 13.33 while the raw 2010 median is 145.0, a ~10.9x
gap, yet 2013-2015 raw and adjusted broadly agree. That is not a clean
single split, so a split-boundary band like KPLC's cannot be derived
A ~3.5x alternation is more consistent with two merged series, a bonus
or rights issue, or a mis-scaled column than with OCR losing a decimal
point. Needs someone with the corporate-action history to resolve.
Until then CARB is reported for review and never written to.
